question.text: Which hydride among the following is less stable?

solution.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>BeH</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> is indeed considered to be less stable compared to other hydrides among the given due to its significant covalent character and electron deficiency. Beryllium, being a small and highly charged cation, attracts the electrons in the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Be</mi><mo>-</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></math> bonds more strongly, resulting in a greater degree of electron sharing between beryllium and hydrogen. This covalent character is in contrast to other alkaline earth metal hydrides, which tend to have more ionic character.
